description: Behavioural obligations for the §16 session primitive — lease lifecycle, renewal, terminal touchpoints, and visibility. Not expressible as schema or deterministic fixtures; proven against a conformant Hub's test suite.
obligation: REGISTRATION (§16.1): (1) The Hub mints `sess_`-namespaced session ids (never client-supplied); a session belongs to the authenticating principal. (2) Registration MUST be rejected for an `agent.id` containing `#` (the §4 address separator — such an id can participate in the inter-agent leg on neither end). (3) `ttl_seconds` MAY be clamped to the advertised bounds, including clamping UP to `sessions.min_ttl_seconds` so every lease comfortably exceeds the §8.7.2 stream hold bound; over-cap registration (`sessions.max_live_per_agent`) -> 429. LEASE + CAS (§16.2/§16.3): (4) A lease is renewed ONLY by client-originated authenticated activity referencing the session — registration, a `?session=` drain, an inbox ack presenting the session (a session-less ack renews NO lease), a stream connect or RECONNECT, or a submit whose `agent.session` names it; a merely-open connection is NOT renewal evidence (§8.7.2). (5) `active -> closed` (explicit DELETE, idempotent) and `active -> expired` (lease lapse, Hub clock §9.5) are terminal and IMMUTABLE under the §7 first-terminal-wins CAS: a close racing an expiry within a sub-ms window yields exactly one terminal state; a renewal racing expiry is evaluated against the same clock in one atomic transition — no post-terminal resurrection. (6) On a session's transition to EITHER terminal, the Hub MUST apply the §14.2 bounce rules to its un-acked session-addressed command mail (dp-022), including the §7 auto-resolutions. KILL-SWITCH (§16.4): (7) Only the owning principal's credential may register, renew, or close its sessions — with one exception: the account's authenticated HUMAN may close any account session (attested, audited); the §14.2 bounce rules then unblock senders waiting on it (the operator's recourse for a stuck agent-addressed ask, §9.1). VISIBILITY (§16.4): (8) Own-session visibility is unconditional — GET /v1/sessions with an agent credential always returns the caller's own live and recent-terminal sessions regardless of policy (a crash-looping agent MUST be able to find and clear stale leases before hitting the live-session cap). (9) Another principal's session id MUST be indistinguishable from unknown; account-wide listing is human-always, same-account-agents only under the advertised `sessions.agent_list_visibility`, cross-account never. (10) Terminal sessions remain readable for `sessions.terminal_retention_seconds`, then are purged; a session read carries the session's §15.1 `last_seen` under exactly these visibility rules.
